This is the eighth public release candidate of the NPMplus Security Fork. It is intended for test servers before a stable release.

### What changed since RC7

- Closed the four findings of the September 16 security quality audit and the six findings of the CrowdSec integration audit. A delegated manager can no longer attach another user's access list by guessing its id, the permission model fails closed on malformed permission strings and anonymous-session sentinels, and the nginx privilege guard now snapshots `forward_port`. Unix-socket and custom upstream destinations (including custom locations and stream upstreams) are administrators-only, and access-list addresses and auth-request upstreams that are not plain addresses are rejected from delegated managers.
- Made the CrowdSec posture fail-closed end to end: the image-seeded bouncer config ships `MODE=stream` and `APPSEC_FAILURE_ACTION=deny`, bouncer and machine key files are created race-free, the daily heal reopens the protected public gate only after the firewall bouncer is active with its ipset rules restored, and the LAPI certificate chain is validated once at the http level (restating it inside the CrowdSec include was a duplicate directive that failed `nginx -t` the moment the include was enabled). Two silent fail-open paths found by the docker attacker simulation are closed: an AppSec outage under `deny` served the CrowdSec Ban page as HTTP 200 (patched in the pinned bouncer source until upstream [lua-cs-bouncer#159](https://github.com/crowdsecurity/lua-cs-bouncer/pull/159) is pinned past), and `deny` without `FALLBACK_REMEDIATION` allowed every request through, which the heal now seeds and the doctor flags.
- Added single-use login challenges and atomic TOTP timestep consumption: a code can no longer be replayed within its validity window. Existing MFA enrollments migrate without resetting their secrets, and the replay state lives outside the MFA metadata so backup-code updates cannot reset it. Access-list usernames containing htpasswd delimiters or control characters are rejected, and malformed legacy records are excluded when the auth file is regenerated.
- Made Attackers the default CrowdSec view: server-paginated source-IP groups, searchable observations, bounded older-history loading, and a chronological investigation drawer whose evidence loads on demand with secret filtering. Local decisions stay distinct from confirmed blocking or compromise. See the [investigation guidance](https://github.com/mangyan1/NPMplus/blob/v2.15.1-mangyan1.rc.8/docs/attacker-investigation.md).
- Fixed the CrowdSec dashboard and backend findings of the September 18 review: bouncer identity is reported with the fork's user agent instead of being relabelled by the LAPI, every LAPI reader answers a stable 502 instead of an unhandled 500, attacker-influenced counter keys can no longer seed a bogus insight row, browser notifications dedupe on stable per-type signal ids and re-fire after a cleared condition, the refresh and pager buttons respond to clicks during background polls, the ASN quick-filter chips use the documented field token, and log lines that a timer repeats are reported once per outage instead of once per tick. A deliberately switched-off nginx observation source now reports `disabled` instead of `unavailable`.
- Reconciled upstream develop through `fce815df` (real merge commit, never squashed): certificate ids a caller cannot see are rejected on create/update across hosts, redirections, dead hosts and streams, new non-admin users default to `hidden` on every resource, and a permission patch that hides access lists while making proxy hosts visible is rejected. nginx moves to 1.31.6 with aws-lc v5.9.0; dependency bumps are taken only once they clear the 7-day pnpm `minimumReleaseAge` supply-chain gate.
- Added CI coverage: a Docker API and browser security workflow running pinned Playwright against the exact checked-out image, a SQLite upgrade regression starting from the pre-replay schema with an existing MFA account, and two new security-invariants rules that fail the build if a permission guard or the fork's package manifests lose their pinned shape.

### Install or update a test VM

Copy and paste the complete command:

```bash
wget -qO setup-npmplus.sh https://github.com/mangyan1/NPMplus/releases/download/v2.15.1-mangyan1.rc.8/setup-npmplus.sh &&
wget -qO setup-npmplus.sh.sha256 https://github.com/mangyan1/NPMplus/releases/download/v2.15.1-mangyan1.rc.8/setup-npmplus.sh.sha256 &&
sha256sum -c setup-npmplus.sh.sha256 &&
sudo bash setup-npmplus.sh
```

Choose **Install NPMplus** for a fresh test VM or **Safe update** for an existing installer-managed test VM. Safe update repairs known configuration drift before the normal snapshot, health-checking, and automatic rollback protection. Existing RC7 test VMs should switch to this release before their next maintenance window: the installer is now v1.59 and its daily heal migrates a seeded fail-open CrowdSec bouncer config to the fail-closed posture on the next run (opt out once with `touch /data/crowdsec/keep-fail-open`). This is otherwise a routine update: the database migration for TOTP replay state runs automatically and no manual steps are required.

Please report problems through [GitHub issues](https://github.com/mangyan1/NPMplus/issues). Report security vulnerabilities privately through the repository Security page.

This fork is based on NPMplus by ZoeyVid and the original Nginx Proxy Manager project by JC21 and contributors. It remains licensed under AGPL-3.0-or-later, with the original MIT-licensed work retained as documented in the repository.
